definition_zh: 神话的；神话中的；神话学的；被讲述得超乎常人的；虚构的
definition_en: belonging to or found in myths, or concerned with the study of myths
core_image: 洞壁上用赭石画出半人半兽的轮廓，火把从下方照上去，影子比真人还高
scene: 展厅的墙面上画着一只半人半兽的怪兽，讲解员正指着它讲古老的来历。 The guide explains the mythological creature painted across the exhibition wall.
sceneCN: 这里 mythological 指「出自神话、属于神话世界的」（第 1 个义项：存在于神话叙事中而非现实里）；句意为讲解员解说展墙上一只神话中的怪兽。可辨识物件：展墙、半人半兽纹样、射灯、讲解牌。

pos.zh: 神话的；神话中的；神话学的；传说化的

derivatives.zh: 基础词 myth 去掉学科形容词后缀 -logical 后剩下的名词核心，语义由「属于神话」收窄为「一则神话故事」
基础词 myth + 希腊 -logia（「讲述、研究」）→ 由「神话故事」偏移为「神话的整体汇集与研究」
基础词 myth + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 由「神话」偏移为「具有神话性质的、传奇般的」
基础词 myth + -ical（形容词后缀）→ 侧重「只存在于神话中、并不真实」
mythology + -ize（动词后缀）→ 由「神话」偏移为「把某人某事讲成神话」
mythologize + -ation（动作名词后缀）→ 偏移为「被神话化的过程」
希腊 mythographos（mythos + graphein「书写」）→ 偏移为「收集并记录神话的人」
mythology + -ist（人名词后缀）→ 偏移为「研究神话的学者」

senses.title: Existing in myth
senses.titleCN: 神话中的，出自神话叙事的
senses.definition: existing in or belonging to a myth rather than to recorded history
senses.definitionCN: 存在于神话之中、属于神话而非有记载的历史
senses.example: The labyrinth was guarded by a mythological beast.
senses.exampleCN: 那座迷宫由一只神话中的怪兽看守。
senses.why: mythos named a told story, and -logical marks whatever belongs to that stock of stories, so the adjective first means found in the tales.
senses.whyCN: mythos 指「被讲述的故事」，-logical 标记属于这类故事的东西，因此这个形容词首先表示「出现在被讲述的故事里」。

senses.title: Belonging to the mythic world
senses.definition: belonging to the whole imagined world of gods, heroes and monsters described by a culture's myths
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个文化的神话所描绘的整个神、英雄与怪兽的想象世界
senses.example: Mythological geography placed the gods on a peak no climber could reach.
senses.exampleCN: 神话地理把众神安置在一座无人能登顶的山峰上。
senses.why: once a culture holds many tales, the adjective covers the shared world they describe, not just a single story.
senses.whyCN: 一个文化一旦拥有许多故事，这个形容词就覆盖它们共同描绘的那个世界，而不只是某一则故事。

senses.title: Relating to the study of myths
senses.definition: concerned with the scholarly collection, classification and comparison of myths
senses.definitionCN: 涉及对神话的学术收集、分类与比较
senses.example: Mythological research compared flood stories from six continents.
senses.exampleCN: 神话学研究比较了六个大洲的洪水故事。
senses.why: the -logia element means telling or study, so the adjective also names the academic approach to myths.
senses.whyCN: -logia 这一成分意为「讲述、研究」，所以这个形容词也指对神话的学术研究取向。

senses.title: Legendary in scale
senses.titleCN: 传说化的，被讲得超乎常人的
senses.definition: described in the exaggerated terms of legend, so that the person or deed is larger than life
senses.definitionCN: 以传说的夸张口吻描述，使人或事迹超出真实尺度
senses.example: His mythological stamina carried him through three days without sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他被传得神乎其神的体力让他三天不睡也撑了下来。
senses.why: storytellers enlarge a real person until the tale fits the shape of myth, and the adjective follows that enlargement.
senses.whyCN: 讲述者会把真实人物放大，直到故事符合神话的形状，这个形容词也随之指这种放大。

senses.title: Fictitious, not real
senses.definition: existing only in imagination; invented and without basis in fact
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于想象中；编造而无事实依据
senses.example: The danger turned out to be mythological, invented to frighten the newcomers.
senses.exampleCN: 那个危险后来证明是虚构的，只是为了吓唬新来的人而编出来的。
senses.why: since myths are stories, calling something mythological can deny it any place in the real world.
senses.whyCN: 既然神话是故事，把某物称作 mythological 就可以否认它在现实世界里有一席之地。

senses.title: Explaining an origin
senses.definition: describing how a natural thing, a custom or a place first came to be
senses.definitionCN: 说明某种自然物、习俗或地方最初如何形成
senses.example: The mythological account of fire traced it to a stolen ember.
senses.exampleCN: 关于火的神话式说法把火追溯到一粒被偷走的余烬。
senses.why: many myths exist precisely to explain origins, so the adjective marks narratives whose purpose is explanation.
senses.whyCN: 许多神话正是为了解释起源而存在，因此这个形容词标出以解释为目的的叙事。

senses.title: Symbolic and archetypal
senses.definition: carrying the symbolic weight of an archetype rather than literal factual detail
senses.definitionCN: 承载原型的象征分量，而非字面的事实细节
senses.example: The mythological mother figure appears in every version of the tale.
senses.exampleCN: 这个神话式的母亲形象出现在故事的每一个版本里。
senses.why: myth speaks in symbols, so what is called mythological often means what carries that symbolic charge.
senses.whyCN: 神话以象征说话，因此被称为 mythological 的往往指承载这种象征分量的东西。

senses.title: As a subject in art
senses.definition: used of painting, music or literature that takes myths as its subject matter
senses.definitionCN: 用于以神话为题材的绘画、音乐或文学
senses.example: The mythological frescoes cover the west wall of the chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 教堂西墙上满是神话题材的壁画。
senses.why: the adjective here labels a category of subject in the arts, not a claim about what exists.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词在艺术中标记的是一个题材类别，而不是对存在与否的断言。

intro.en: Mythological is built on Greek mythos 'word, speech, story' plus the suffix -logia 'telling, study', and reached English through Late Latin mythologicus and French mythologique. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mythological 由希腊 mythos「言说、故事」加后缀 -logia「讲述、研究」构成，经晚期拉丁 mythologicus 与法语 mythologique 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mythos meant 'word, speech, tale'. Its deeper origin is not established: no Indo-European source has been demonstrated, and the often suggested link with a verb of speaking is a hypothesis rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: mythos 意为「言语、讲述、故事」。其更早来源未得到证明：没有任何印欧语来源被证实；常有人把它与某个「说」的动词联系起来，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Mythos plus -logia, from logos 'word, account', produced mythologia 'the telling of tales, legend'. The compound names both the activity of narrating and the body of tales told.
items.cn: mythos 加 -logia（来自 logos「言说、道理」）构成 mythologia「讲故事、传说」，既指叙述活动，也指被讲述的那一批故事。

items.en: The adjective mythologikos described a person skilled in telling tales, and later what belongs to tales of gods and heroes.
items.cn: 形容词 mythologikos 最初形容擅长讲故事的人，后来指属于神与英雄故事的东西。

items.en: Late Latin mythologicus was formed directly on the Greek adjective; it is a borrowed learned word, not an inherited Latin relative.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 mythologicus 直接依希腊形容词构成；它是借入的学术词，而非拉丁语固有同族词。

items.en: French mythologique passed into English as mythological in the seventeenth century, first in the sense of relating to myths and their study.
items.cn: 法语 mythologique 在十七世纪进入英语成为 mythological，最初指与神话及其研究相关。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Greek origin of mythos is unsettled and the exact first English date is not recorded, so any older form offered for mythos is a reconstructed form rather than attested evidence.
items.cn: 来源不确定：mythos 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，英语首见的确切年代也没有记录，因此凡为 mythos 给出的更早形式均属重构形式，而非有书证的材料。

note.en: Group one holds the myth family and its closest story-words, which are constantly swapped; group two holds words that deny reality or carry symbolic meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是 myth 词族及其最近的故事类词，最易互相替换出错；第二组是否认现实或承载象征意义的词。

entries.definition: Of or like myth, often used of a person or event raised to legendary stature; it leans toward the symbolic rather than toward one particular tale.
entries.definitionCN: 属于或类似神话的，常用于被抬到传奇地位的人或事件；侧重象征性，而非某一则具体故事。

entries.definition: Chiefly means imagined or fictitious; it overlaps mythic but pushes harder toward 'does not exist'.
entries.definitionCN: 主要指想象中或虚构的；与 mythic 有重叠，但更强调「并不存在」。

entries.definition: The noun names a traditional tale or a widely believed falsehood; the adjective describes what such a tale contains, the noun names the tale.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指传统故事或广为相信的谬见；形容词描述这类故事里的东西，名词则指故事本身。

entries.definition: A body of myths, or the study of them; it names the whole set, while mythological describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指神话的整体汇集或对神话的研究；它命名整套，而 mythological 描述属于这套的东西。

entries.definition: A story about a human hero, usually with a historical kernel; myth concerns gods and origins, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 关于人类英雄的故事，通常有一点历史内核；神话关注神与起源，二者不能互换。

entries.definition: From fabula 'story': belonging to fable, hence incredible; it stresses the unbelievable rather than the sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 fabula「故事」：属于寓言的，因而难以置信；它强调不可信，而非神圣性。

entries.definition: Plainly 'made up'; it denies reality without implying any sacred or explanatory function.
entries.definitionCN: 直白地表示「编造的」；它否认现实性，但不含神圣或解释功能。

entries.definition: Said of a story that circulates as true but is probably not; it targets credibility rather than genre.
entries.definitionCN: 指以真实之名流传、却很可能不真的故事；它针对可信度，而非文类。

entries.definition: Carrying a meaning beyond the literal; myths are symbolic, but a symbolic gesture need not come from any myth.
entries.definitionCN: 承载字面之外的意义；神话是象征性的，但象征性的举动未必出自神话。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mythos 'story' + -logical 'pertaining to': pertaining to told stories.
normal.cn: mythos「故事」+ -logical「与……相关」：与被人讲述的故事相关。

normal.en: The family runs myth, mythic, mythical, mythology, mythologist, mythologize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 myth、mythic、mythical、mythology、mythologist、mythologize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday uses: mythological figure, mythological creature, mythological theme.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常用法：神话人物、神话生物、神话主题。

normal.en: The same -logia element appears in theology, biology and geology, each naming a field of telling or study.
normal.cn: 同一个 -logia 成分出现在 theology、biology 与 geology 中，都指某个讲述或研究的领域。

normal.en: The story stock also yields mythographer and mythography, words for collecting and writing down myths.
normal.cn: 同一批故事还衍生出 mythographer 与 mythography，指收集并记录神话的人与工作。

abstract.en: Picture a stone wall lit from below, where every painted figure casts a shadow taller than a person.
abstract.cn: 想象一面被下方火光照亮的石壁，上面每个画出的形象都投下比人更高的影子。

abstract.en: Picture a map that marks a mountain where gods live, yet shows no path leading there.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，标着神居住的山，却没有画出任何一条通到那里的路。

abstract.en: Picture a man retold so many times that the telling has made him a head taller than he was.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人被反复讲述，讲到后来他比本人高出了一个头。

examples.en: The mosaic shows a mythological hunt in which a goddess stops the arrows in midair.
examples.cn: 这幅镶嵌画描绘一场神话中的狩猎，一位女神让箭停在半空。

examples.en: Scholars treat the flood narrative as mythological rather than as a weather report.
examples.cn: 学者把那则洪水叙事当作神话来看，而不是当作气象记录。

examples.en: His reputed speed on the field has become almost mythological among local fans.
examples.cn: 他在球场上传说般的速度，在当地球迷中几乎已成神话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「myth（神话）+ 连接元音 + logical（学科形容词后缀）」——属于神话那一类 → 神话的、神话中的

root: 希腊 mythos「言说、故事」+ -logia（来自 logos「言说、道理」）「讲述、研究」；mythos 更早来源不确定。英语 mythological 经晚期拉丁 mythologicus 与法语 mythologique 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a told story first fills a whole imagined world, then becomes an object of study, then lends its exaggerated scale and its unreality to ordinary speech, and finally becomes a subject category in art.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个走向展开：被讲述的故事先撑起一整个想象世界，再成为研究对象，随后把夸张的尺度与「不真实」借给日常语言，最后成为艺术中的一个题材类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a story told about gods, and the shadow it casts over the real world.
core.cn: 核心意象：一则关于神的故事，以及它投在现实世界上的影子。

branches.en: THE STORY AND ITS WORLD: one tale first, then the whole imagined geography that holds all the tales together.
branches.cn: 故事与其世界：先是一则故事，再是容纳全部故事的整个想象地理。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the -logia element turns the tales into objects that can be collected, compared and classified.
branches.cn: 研究：-logia 这一成分把这些故事变成可收集、可比较、可分类的对象。

branches.en: SCALE AND REALITY: telling enlarges a figure, and calling something mythological can also be a way of denying that it exists.
branches.cn: 尺度与真实：讲述会放大人物，而称之为神话也可以是在否认它存在。

branches.en: EXPLANATION: a story that answers where fire, seasons or customs first came from.
branches.cn: 解释：回答火、季节或习俗最初从何而来的故事。

branches.en: SYMBOL AND SUBJECT: the archetype carries meaning, and the arts take myths as a category of subject matter.
branches.cn: 象征与题材：原型承载意义，艺术则把神话当作一个题材类别。

intro.en: Mythological can be read in parts: a Greek noun for a told story, a linking vowel, and a suffix that names a field of study.
intro.cn: mythological 可以按部分读出：一个指「被讲述的故事」的希腊名词、一个连接元音，以及一个指研究领域的后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no inherited Latin family here. The stock is Greek: mythos reached Latin only as a borrowed noun, and mythologicus is a Late Latin adjective shaped on the Greek model, so no genuine Latin cognate exists.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语固有词族。其来源是希腊语：mythos 只作为借词进入拉丁语，mythologicus 是依希腊范式构成的晚期拉丁形容词，因此不存在真正的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The root carries the idea of something spoken aloud.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「被大声讲出来」的意思。

items.example: The vowel keeps the compound pronounceable.
items.exampleCN: 这个元音让复合词读得顺口。

items.meaning: pertaining to a field of study
items.example: The suffix turns a subject into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一个学科变成形容词。

items.meaning: a body of myths or their study
items.meaningCN: 神话的汇集或对神话的研究
items.example: The mythology of the region survives in song.
items.exampleCN: 该地区的神话靠歌谣留存下来。

items.example: The battle took on a mythic colour.
items.exampleCN: 那场战斗带上了一层神话色彩。

items.example: The mythical island appears on old charts.
items.exampleCN: 那座神话中的岛屿出现在旧海图上。

items.example: Later writers mythologized the general's retreat.
items.exampleCN: 后来的作家把这位将军的撤退写成了神话。

items.example: The mythologization of the frontier took a generation.
items.exampleCN: 边疆被神话化用了一代人的时间。

items.meaning: a collector and writer of myths
items.example: The mythographer listed three versions of the birth story.
items.exampleCN: 这位神话记录者列出了这个诞生故事的三个版本。

items.example: The mythologist traced the motif across languages.
items.exampleCN: 这位神话学者跨越语言追踪了这个母题。

definition_zh: 模拟；仿真；假装；模仿
definition_en: to imitate the appearance or conditions of something, sometimes in order to deceive
core_image: 飞行模拟舱里，仪表和真飞机一样转动，但窗外只是一块屏幕
scene: 飞行训练中心，学员在模拟舱里练习迫降。教官说： The simulator can simulate an engine failure at 30,000 feet.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 simulate 是「模拟、仿真」（第 2、4 个义项：用模型重现真实条件）；句意：模拟器可以模拟三万英尺高空的发动机失效。图中可辨识物件：模拟舱、仪表盘、球形屏幕、教员座椅。

derivatives.zh: 模拟；仿真；假装
模拟器；仿真装置
模拟的；仿真的；假装的
模拟的；有模仿作用的

senses.title: To pretend: putting on a false front
senses.titleCN: 假装：摆出不真实的样子
senses.definition: to pretend to have a feeling, illness or quality that one does not really have
senses.definitionCN: 假装拥有某种实际并不存在的情感、疾病或品质
senses.example: He simulated illness to avoid the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 他装病以逃避考试。
senses.why: Latin simulare could mean both 'to make like' and 'to feign'. The second sense survives: the outer surface is copied, while the inner state is missing. Simulation is a likeness with no substance behind it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 simulare 既可表示“使相像”，也可表示“假装”。第二个义项活了下来：外层表面被复制，而内在状态缺席。假装是一种背后没有实质的相似。

senses.title: To reproduce real conditions
senses.definition: to create conditions that copy the important features of a real situation, usually for study or training
senses.definitionCN: 创造复制了真实情境重要特征的条件，通常用于研究或训练
senses.example: The chamber simulates the pressure at high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这个舱室模拟高海拔的气压。
senses.why: Here the copy is honest: the aim is not to deceive but to reproduce. Engineers keep the variables that matter and drop the rest, so the model can be tested safely.
senses.whyCN: 这里的复制是诚实的：目的不是欺骗，而是重现。工程师保留真正重要的变量，舍弃其余部分，从而能安全地测试模型。

senses.title: To imitate an appearance or sound
senses.definition: to copy the look, sound or manner of something so that it resembles the original
senses.definitionCN: 复制某物的外观、声音或举止，使其像原物
senses.example: The actor simulated the old man's walk.
senses.exampleCN: 演员模仿了那位老人的步态。
senses.why: The Latin verb was used for making a copy of a thing. In this sense the imitation is visible and often skilful, and the question of deceit does not arise.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本就用于“给某物做一个复本”。在这个义项里，模仿是可见的、常常很技巧性，是否欺骗的问题并不出现。

senses.title: Computer simulation
senses.definition: to run a model on a computer so that it reproduces the behaviour of a real system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机上运行模型，使其重现真实系统的行为
senses.example: The program simulates how heat spreads through the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 该程序模拟热量如何在墙体中传导。
senses.why: A computer can carry a model through thousands of steps that would be too slow or too dangerous to run in reality. Simulation here means letting a formal description act out the process.
senses.whyCN: 计算机能把模型推进成千上万步，而在现实中跑这些步骤要么太慢、要么太危险。这里的仿真，就是让一份形式化描述“演”出整个过程。

senses.title: Training by simulated practice
senses.definition: to let a learner practise in an artificial setting that reproduces the pressures of the real task
senses.definitionCN: 让学习者在复现真实任务压力的人造环境中练习
senses.example: Pilots train on simulators before flying real aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在驾驶真飞机之前先在模拟器上训练。
senses.why: The point of simulated flight is that mistakes are cheap. The copy is close enough to transfer skill, yet detached enough to absorb failure.
senses.whyCN: 模拟飞行的意义在于犯错的代价很低。这个复本足够接近真实，使技能可以迁移；又足够脱离真实，使失败可以被吸收。

senses.title: To feign an attitude
senses.definition: to display an emotion or interest that one does not feel, usually for social reasons
senses.definitionCN: 表现出并未真正感受到的情绪或兴趣，通常出于社交原因
senses.example: She simulated interest in the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 她假装对讲座感兴趣。
senses.why: Social life often requires the surface of an emotion without its substance. The word marks exactly that gap: the visible sign is produced, the inner state is not.
senses.whyCN: 社交生活常常需要情绪的表面，而不需要它的实质。这个词标记的正是那道缝隙：可见的信号被制造出来，内在状态却不存在。

senses.title: To model an outcome
senses.definition: to use a model to work out what would happen under given conditions, before the event occurs
senses.definitionCN: 用模型推算出在给定条件下会发生什么，且发生在事件之前
senses.example: Economists simulated the effect of the tax cut.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家模拟了减税的效果。
senses.why: The model is a stand-in that can be pushed ahead of reality. Simulating an outcome is a way of trying the future at low cost.
senses.whyCN: 模型是现实的替身，可以被推到现实之前。模拟结果，就是用低成本的方式先“试一遍”未来。

senses.title: Simulating biological conditions
senses.definition: in biology and medicine, to reproduce the chemical or physical conditions of a living system
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学与医学中，重现生命系统的化学或物理条件
senses.example: The device simulates the acidity of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 该装置模拟胃部的酸度。
senses.why: Living systems are hard to open and hard to control. A simulated environment keeps the relevant parameters while removing the complexity that would confound the experiment.
senses.whyCN: 生命系统难以打开、也难以控制。模拟环境保留相关参数，同时去掉会干扰实验的复杂性。

senses.title: Simulated: the adjective of the artificial
senses.definition: the past participle works as an adjective meaning 'made to resemble something real, and not real itself'
senses.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，意为“被做成像真的、但本身并非真的”
senses.example: The aircraft landed on a simulated runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机降落在一条模拟跑道上。
senses.why: Once the participle becomes an adjective, the 'as if' is packed into a single word: simulated leather, simulated flavour, simulated emergency. The likeness is the point, and the absence of the original is understood.
senses.whyCN: 当分词变成形容词，“仿佛”就被压缩进一个词里：simulated leather、simulated flavour、simulated emergency。相似本身就是重点，而原物的缺席则是不言自明的。

intro.en: Simulate comes from Latin simulare 'to make like, imitate, represent', built on similis 'like'. English first used it in the 1620s for pretending; the technical sense 'reproduce conditions with a model' is a 20th-century development.
intro.cn: simulate 来自拉丁语 simulare“使相像、模仿、再现”，建立在 similis“像”之上。英语在 17 世纪 20 年代最早用它表示“假装”；“用模型重现条件”的技术义则是 20 世纪的发展。

items.en: Similis meant 'like, resembling'. It is the adjective behind the whole family, and its older relative semol 'together' points to PIE *sem- 'one, together'.
items.cn: similis 意为“相像的”。它是整个词族背后的形容词，其更早的亲属 semol“一起”指向原始印欧语 *sem-“一、一起”。

items.en: Simulare meant 'to make like, copy, imitate, represent', and also 'to pretend'. The verb could describe an artist copying a face or a person faking a feeling.
items.cn: simulare 意为“使相像、复制、模仿、再现”，也可表示“假装”。这个动词既能描述画家复制一张脸，也能描述一个人伪造一种情感。

items.en: The past participle simulatus 'made like, imitated, feigned' supplied the stem for the English verb. The Latin supine form simulatum also underlies the noun simulation.
items.cn: 过去分词 simulatus“被弄得相像的、被模仿的、被假装的”为英语动词提供了词干。拉丁语动名词形式 simulatum 也是名词 simulation 的基础。

items.en: English simulate is first recorded in the 1620s with the sense 'to feign, pretend'. It was either a back-formation from simulation or a direct borrowing of the Latin participle.
items.cn: 英语 simulate 最早记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，意为“假装、装作”。它要么是从 simulation 逆构而来，要么是直接借用了拉丁语分词。

items.en: The modern technical sense 'to imitate the working of a system, especially with a model or computer' is recorded from the mid-20th century (c. 1947), alongside the growth of simulators.
items.cn: 现代技术义“模仿某一系统的运作，尤指用模型或计算机”记录于 20 世纪中期（约 1947），与模拟器的兴起同步。

items.en: Simulation, simulator and simulated now cover engineering, medicine, economics and games. The old polarity survives: the copy may be offered as a tool, or offered as a deception.
items.cn: simulation、simulator、simulated 如今覆盖工程、医学、经济学与游戏。旧的二元性仍然存在：这个复本既可以作为工具提供，也可以作为骗局提供。

note.en: The look-alike group is the simul- family; the near-meaning group compares verbs of copying and pretending. Watch the difference between an honest model and a deliberate lie.
note.cn: 形近组是 simul- 词族；近义组比较表示复制与假装的动词。注意“诚实的模型”与“有意的谎言”之间的差别。

entries.definition: the act or result of simulating; a model that reproduces a real process. It is the noun of simulate.
entries.definitionCN: 模拟的行为或结果；重现真实过程的模型。它是 simulate 的名词。

entries.definition: a device or program that simulates conditions for training or study. It is the thing that does the simulating.
entries.definitionCN: 为训练或研究而模拟条件的装置或程序。它是执行模拟的那个东西。

entries.definition: to hide one's real feelings by pretending the opposite. The prefix dis- reverses the direction of the pretence.
entries.definitionCN: 通过装作相反的样子来掩盖真实情感。前缀 dis- 反转了伪装的方向。

entries.definition: to copy someone's actions or manner, often to learn or to entertain. It does not imply deception.
entries.definitionCN: 复制他人的行为或举止，常用于学习或娱乐。它不暗示欺骗。

entries.definition: to copy the sound or movement of something, often in a playful or exaggerated way.
entries.definitionCN: 复制某物的声音或动作，常带有戏仿或夸张。

entries.definition: to pretend to have a feeling or condition. It is close to the oldest sense of simulate.
entries.definitionCN: 假装拥有某种情感或状况。它接近 simulate 最古老的义项。

entries.definition: to try to equal or surpass someone by imitating their success. It adds striving, not pretence.
entries.definitionCN: 通过模仿他人的成功来试图赶上或超越。它增加了努力，而不是伪装。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a flight simulator, a fake cough, a computer model of heat, a simulated runway.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：飞行模拟器、假装的咳嗽、热的计算机模型、模拟跑道。

normal.en: Similis is 'like': to simulate is to make something look or behave like the real thing.
normal.cn: similis 就是“像”：simulate 就是让某物看起来或表现得像真的。

normal.en: A flight simulator copies the cockpit but not the sky: the relevant parts are real, the danger is not.
normal.cn: 飞行模拟器复制了驾驶舱，却没有复制天空：相关部分是真实的，危险则不是。

normal.en: Simulate an illness is to fake it; simulate a climate is to model it. One deceives, the other studies.
normal.cn: simulate an illness 是装病；simulate a climate 是建模。前者骗人，后者研究。

normal.en: The noun pair: simulation is the process, simulator is the machine.
normal.cn: 名词配对：simulation 是过程，simulator 是机器。

normal.en: Simulated leather, simulated flavour: the adjective tells you the real material is absent.
normal.cn: simulated leather、simulated flavour：这个形容词告诉你真正的材料并不在场。

abstract.en: One schema: LIKE → COPY → PRETEND → REPRODUCE → MODEL → TEST.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：像 → 复制 → 假装 → 重现 → 建模 → 检验。

abstract.en: Word-family check: similar (adj.) → simulate (v.) → simulation (n.) → simulator (n.) → simulated (adj.).
abstract.cn: 词族检查：similar（形）→ simulate（动）→ simulation（名）→ simulator（名）→ simulated（形）。

abstract.en: Contrast: imitate copies behaviour, mimic copies sound, feign fakes a state, emulate copies in order to rival.
abstract.cn: 对照：imitate 复制行为，mimic 复制声音，feign 伪造状态，emulate 为竞争而复制。

examples.en: The program simulates how the virus spreads through a city.
examples.cn: 该程序模拟病毒如何在一座城市中传播。

examples.en: He simulated a headache to leave the meeting early.
examples.cn: 他假装头痛，以便提前离开会议。

examples.en: The astronauts trained in a simulated weightless environment.
examples.cn: 宇航员在模拟失重环境中训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: “西米尤勒特”——西米（粒）尤（其）勒（住）特（像）→ 把东西勒成一样 → simulate 模拟、假装

root: 源自拉丁语 simulare“使相像、模仿、假装”，由 similis“相像的”派生；过去分词 simulatus 进入英语。核心是“做出一个像真的复本”，既可用于诚实的建模，也可用于欺骗性的假装。

sensesIntro.en: Simulate starts from a copy. The oldest sense is pretence: a person fakes an illness or an interest. The same act becomes respectable when the copy is meant to teach or to predict: an altitude chamber reproduces pressure, a computer runs a model, a pilot practises on a simulator, an economist tries the future before it arrives. The adjective simulated then carries the whole idea in one word: made to resemble something real, and not real itself.
sensesIntro.cn: simulate 的起点是一个复本。最古老的义项是伪装：一个人装病、装感兴趣。当复本被用来教学或预测时，同一个动作就变得正当：高压舱重现气压，计算机跑模型，飞行员在模拟器上练习，经济学家在未来到来之前先试一遍。形容词 simulated 则用一个词承载整个观念：被做成像真的，而本身并非真的。

core.en: Making a likeness: copying a surface, a condition or a process, with or without intent to deceive.
core.cn: 制造相似：复制表面、条件或过程，可能有意欺骗，也可能没有。

branches.en: PRETENCE: faking an illness, and faking an attitude, where the inner state is missing.
branches.cn: 伪装：装病与装态度，内在状态缺席。

branches.en: IMITATION: copying a walk, a voice or a manner for display.
branches.cn: 模仿：为展示而复制步态、声音或举止。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION: recreating real physical or biological conditions for study.
branches.cn: 重现：为研究而再造真实的物理或生理条件。

branches.en: MODELLING: running a system or an outcome through a model, often on a computer.
branches.cn: 建模：用模型推演系统或结果，常在计算机上运行。

branches.en: TRAINING AND ARTIFICE: simulated practice, and the adjective for things that only resemble the real.
branches.cn: 训练与人造：模拟练习，以及表示“只是像真的”的形容词。

intro.en: Simulate sits in the simil-/simul- family. The items below move from the Latin verb through the modern technical nouns to the adjective of artifice.
intro.cn: simulate 位于 simil-/simul- 词族中。下列条目从拉丁动词出发，经过现代技术名词，到达表示“人造”的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis 'like' gives simulare 'make like', whose participle simulatus supplies English simulate. Simulacrum adds the idea of a mere image or shadow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 similis“像”派生出 simulare“使相像”，其分词 simulatus 提供英语 simulate。simulacrum 则加入“仅是影像或影子”的意思。

items.meaning: the act or result of simulating
items.example: The simulation took six hours to run.
items.exampleCN: 这次仿真运行了六个小时。

items.meaning: a device or program that simulates
items.exampleCN: 模拟器重现驾驶舱条件。

items.example: They tested the material in simulated sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 他们在模拟阳光下测试该材料。

items.meaningCN: 模拟性的；有模仿作用的
items.example: The game has a simulative function.
items.exampleCN: 这款游戏具有模拟功能。

items.meaning: to conceal one's feelings by pretence

items.exampleCN: 她的镇定完全是装出来的。
这个寓言通过比喻起作用。

items.meaning: an image or imitation that lacks substance
items.meaningCN: 影像；幻影；徒有其表的东西
items.example: The town was a simulacrum of a real city.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇只是一座真实城市的仿像。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被弄得相像的；被假装的

definition_zh: 终止；结束；期满；解雇
definition_en: to bring something to an end, to come to an end, to end a person's employment, or to stop at a fixed limit
core_image: 田野尽头立着一块界石：走到它，路就到此为止。
scene: 这里指「终止」。 The lease terminates at the end of March.
sceneCN: 这里 terminate 是「（合同）到期终止」（第 2 个义项：自行结束、期满）；句意：租约在三月底到期。场景要点：租约文件、翻到三月的日历、交回的钥匙、腾空的房间。

derivatives.zh: 终止；结束；解雇
终点站；终端；末期的
终点站；终点
可终止的；有期限的

senses.title: Bring something to an end
senses.titleCN: 使终止：把进程推到界石前
senses.definition: to cause something such as a project, process, or agreement to end
senses.definitionCN: 使项目、进程或协议等结束
senses.example: The company terminated the project after the trial failed.
senses.exampleCN: 试验失败后，公司终止了这个项目。
senses.why: Latin terminus was a boundary stone. To terminate is to drive an activity up to that stone and stop it there, with someone doing the stopping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 terminus 是界石。terminate 就是把一项活动推到那块石头前并停下，而且是由某人来停。

senses.title: Come to an end by itself
senses.titleCN: 自行结束：走到期限就到了
senses.definition: to end naturally at a fixed time, as a contract or period does
senses.definitionCN: 在固定时间自然结束，如合同或期限
senses.example: The contract terminates automatically after five years.
senses.exampleCN: 合同五年后自动终止。
senses.why: The same stone marks the limit, but now nobody pushes. The agreement reaches its boundary on its own, so the verb becomes intransitive.
senses.whyCN: 同一块界石标出界限，但这次没人推。协议自己走到边界，于是动词变成不及物用法。

senses.title: Dismiss someone from a job
senses.titleCN: 解雇：把人的任职期截断
senses.definition: to end a person's employment, especially as an official or euphemistic act
senses.definitionCN: 结束某人的雇佣关系，尤指以正式或委婉的说法
senses.example: He was terminated for repeated safety violations.
senses.exampleCN: 他因多次违反安全规定而被解雇。
senses.why: A job is a period with a boundary. Cutting it short means bringing that person's term to its limit before the natural date, so the word is used as a cold official euphemism.
senses.whyCN: 任职是一段有边界的时间。提前截断，就是把此人的任期在自然到期前推到界限，因此这个词被用作冷冰冰的官方委婉语。

senses.title: Of a route: end at a place
senses.titleCN: 到站：线路在界石处结束
senses.definition: of a bus, train, or line, to have a particular place as its final stop
senses.definitionCN: 指公交、火车或线路以某地为终点站
senses.example: The line terminates at a small station in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这条线路终止于山间的一个小站。
senses.why: Here the boundary is a real place on the ground. The rails stop where the terminus stands, and the word is entirely spatial again.
senses.whyCN: 这里的边界是地面上真实的地点。铁轨在终点站所在处停止，词义又完全回到了空间。

senses.title: To end a pregnancy
senses.titleCN: 终止妊娠：以医学术语截断
senses.definition: to end a pregnancy deliberately, used as a medical and legal euphemism
senses.definitionCN: 有意结束妊娠，用作医学与法律上的委婉说法
senses.example: The clinic offers counselling before a pregnancy is terminated.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在终止妊娠前提供咨询。
senses.why: A pregnancy is treated as a process with a term. Ending it early is again stopping before the natural boundary, and the neutral Latin word keeps the statement clinical.
senses.whyCN: 妊娠被当作一段有期限的进程。提前结束，仍是在自然边界前停下；中性的拉丁词让表述保持临床语气。

senses.title: To end a process or connection
senses.titleCN: 终结进程：机器里的界石
senses.definition: of a program, process, or connection, to stop running or close
senses.definitionCN: 指程序、进程或连接停止运行或关闭
senses.example: The program terminates when the last window closes.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个窗口关闭时，程序就终止。
senses.why: Software borrows the boundary stone for the point at which execution stops. The metaphor is exact: a process runs until it hits its end marker.
senses.whyCN: 软件借用了界石，指执行停止的那一点。这个比喻很精确：进程一直运行，直到撞上结束标记。

senses.title: To end in a particular result
senses.definition: to have a particular result or conclusion, especially after a long process
senses.definitionCN: 尤指经过漫长过程后得到某种结果或结局
senses.example: The dispute terminated in a settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端以和解告终。
senses.why: When a path ends at a stone, what lies at the stone is the outcome. Terminate in names that outcome, turning a spatial end into a logical conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 当一条路终止于界石，石头所在处的东西就是结果。terminate in 指出的正是那个结果，把空间的终点变成逻辑的结论。

senses.title: To be bounded by something
senses.definition: to have a particular line, place, or feature as a boundary or ending point
senses.definitionCN: 以某条线、某个地点或特征为边界或终点
senses.example: The property terminates at the river bank.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地产以河岸为界。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal use: a piece of land stops where the boundary marker stands. Everything else in the word grows from this image.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最字面的用法：一块土地在界石所在处停止。这个词的其他义项都从这幅图像生长出来。

intro.en: Terminate comes from Latin terminus, the stone that marked a boundary, and terminare, to set a bound. English first used it as an adjective and later as a verb meaning to reach or set the limit.
intro.cn: terminate 来自拉丁语 terminus“标出边界的石头”和 terminare“设定边界”。英语先把它用作形容词，后来才用作“到达或设定界限”的动词。

items.en: Terminus was a boundary stone or marker between fields. It was also the name of the Roman god who protected boundaries.
items.cn: terminus 是田地之间标界的石头或标记，也是保护边界的罗马神祇之名。

items.en: Terminare meant to set a bound, limit, or end, and by extension to finish. The verb is built directly on the stone.
items.cn: terminare 意为设定边界、限度或终点，引申为完成。这个动词直接建立在“界石”之上。

items.en: The past participle terminatus meant bounded or finished. English kept it as an adjective before the verb became common.
items.cn: 过去分词 terminatus 意为“有边界的、已完成的”。在动词流行之前，英语先把它当作形容词使用。

items.en: Terminate appears in 15c. as an adjective meaning limited or bounded, and in the 16c. as a verb meaning to bring to an end.
items.cn: 15 世纪 terminate 作形容词，意为“有限的、有边界的”；16 世纪作动词，意为“使结束”。

items.en: Railways gave the word its familiar station sense: a line terminates where the track ends. The noun terminus carries the same stone.
items.cn: 铁路赋予这个词熟悉的站点义：线路在铁轨尽头终止。名词 terminus 承载着同一块界石。

items.en: The 20c. added the computing sense and made the employment sense a standard euphemism. The boundary image survives unchanged underneath.
items.cn: 20 世纪增加了计算机义，并使“解雇”义成为标准委婉语。底层的边界意象原封不动地保留着。

note.en: The first group shares the terminus root and its suffixes; the second separates the many ways an action can stop.
note.cn: 第一组共享 terminus 词根及其后缀；第二组区分“停止”这一动作的多种方式。

entries.definition: the act of ending something, or the end itself. It is also the formal word for dismissal.
entries.definitionCN: 结束某物的行为或结束本身；也是“解雇”的正式说法。

entries.definition: the end point of a journey or a device at the end of a line; as an adjective, at the end or fatal.
entries.definitionCN: 旅程的终点或线路末端的设备；作形容词指末端的、致命的。

entries.definition: able to be ended, especially of a contract with a fixed notice period.
entries.definitionCN: 可终止的，尤指附有固定通知期的合同。

entries.definition: seeming to have no end, usually because it is boring or long. The prefix denies the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 似乎没有尽头的，通常因为冗长乏味。前缀否定了边界。

entries.definition: to stop or finish. It is the plain word and can be transitive or intransitive without any official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 停止或结束。它最普通，可及物也可不及物，没有官方语气。

entries.definition: to bring something to a deliberate close, such as a speech, deal, or investigation. It often implies a proper ending.
entries.definitionCN: 有意识地结束演讲、交易或调查，常含“圆满收尾”之意。

entries.definition: of a contract, licence, or period, to end because its time is up. It matches the intransitive sense of terminate.
entries.definitionCN: 指合同、执照或期限因时间到期而结束，对应 terminate 的不及物义。

entries.definition: to remove someone from a job or duty. It is the direct human word where terminate is the official euphemism.
entries.definitionCN: 解除某人的职务或工作。它是直接说人的词，而 terminate 是官方委婉语。

entries.definition: to stop happening or doing, often used of sounds, activities, or legal orders. It is more formal and less spatial.
entries.definitionCN: 停止发生或停止做，常用于声音、活动或法律命令。它更正式，空间感更弱。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin terminus 'boundary stone' and terminare 'set a bound'. Family words termination, terminal, terminus, terminable, interminable.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 terminus“界石”与 terminare“设定边界”。词族为 termination、terminal、terminus、terminable、interminable。

normal.en: Terminus is a stone in a field; terminate is stopping at that stone.
normal.cn: terminus 是田里的一块石头；terminate 就是在石头前停下。

normal.en: A terminal is where the rails meet the stone; a termination is where the contract does.
normal.cn: terminal 是铁轨遇到界石的地方；termination 是合同遇到界石的地方。

normal.en: Interminable denies the stone: a speech with no visible boundary.
normal.cn: interminable 否定了那块石头：一场看不到边界的演讲。

normal.en: Terminate at is a place on the ground; terminate in is a result at the end.
normal.cn: terminate at 是地面上的地点；terminate in 是终点处的结果。

normal.en: Being terminated is having your work period cut at the stone early.
normal.cn: 被 terminate，就是你的工作期限在石头前被提前截断。

abstract.en: Every ending is a boundary that someone agreed to call final.
abstract.cn: 每个结束，都是有人同意称之为最终的边界。

abstract.en: The stone does not stop the field; it only tells you where the field stops being yours.
abstract.cn: 石头并不让田野停止，它只是告诉你田野到哪里不再属于你。

abstract.en: We need termini not because roads are long, but because otherwise we never know when to stop walking.
abstract.cn: 我们需要终点，不是因为路长，而是否则永远不知道该在何时停下。

examples.en: The airline terminated the route after demand collapsed.
examples.cn: 需求骤降后，航空公司终止了这条航线。

examples.en: His contract terminated when the funding ran out.
examples.cn: 资金耗尽时，他的合同到期终止。

examples.en: The pipeline terminates at a storage tank near the coast.
examples.cn: 这条管道终止于海岸附近的一座储罐。

dict_mnemonic.text: “特迷你特”——特别迷你的特工走到田头界石就停下 → terminate 终止、到终点

root: 源自拉丁语 terminus“界石、边界标记”与 terminare“设定边界”；核心是“走到界石处为止”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of terminate, all one stone: an activity, a contract, a job, a route, a pregnancy, a process, or a dispute reaches its boundary and stops there.
sensesIntro.cn: terminate 的八个义项都围绕同一块界石：活动、合同、工作、线路、妊娠、进程或争端走到自己的边界，就在那里停止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone at the far edge of a field.
core.cn: 核心意象：田野尽头的一块界石。

branches.en: CUTTING AND ARRIVING: one party can push a thing to the stone, or the thing can reach it by itself.
branches.cn: 截断与抵达：一方可以把事情推到石头前，事情也可以自己走到那里。

branches.en: EMPLOYMENT: a job is a term with a boundary, and terminating cuts that term early.
branches.cn: 雇佣：工作是一段有边界的任期，terminate 就是提前截断这段任期。

branches.en: PLACES: a route and a property both stop at a real stone on the ground.
branches.cn: 地点：线路与地产都停在地面上真实的那块石头处。

branches.en: DELIBERATE STOPS: a pregnancy and a process are ended on purpose, one by medicine and one by code.
branches.cn: 有意停止：妊娠与进程都是被有意结束，一个靠医学，一个靠代码。

branches.en: OUTCOME: whatever lies at the stone when the path ends is the result it terminates in.
branches.cn: 结局：路走完时石头所在处的东西，就是它 terminate in 的结果。

intro.en: Terminate's family is built on Latin terminus. Suffixes make nouns of state and agents, -able marks what can be ended, and in- denies the boundary.
intro.cn: terminate 的词族建立在拉丁语 terminus 上。后缀构成状态名词与形容词，-able 表示“可被结束”，in- 否定边界。

latinIntro.en: The core Latin forms are terminus 'boundary stone', terminare 'to bound', and terminatus 'bounded'. Exterminare adds ex- 'out beyond'.
latinIntro.cn: 核心拉丁形式是 terminus“界石”、terminare“设界”、terminatus“有边界的”。exterminare 则加 ex-“向外越过”。

items.meaning: the act of ending something, or the end itself
items.meaningCN: 终止；结束；结束的行为（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The termination of the lease requires sixty days' notice.
items.exampleCN: 终止租约需要提前六十天通知。

items.meaning: at the end of a line, or the end point itself
items.meaningCN: 末端的；终点站；终端（-al 构成形容词与名词）
items.example: We met at the bus terminal.
items.exampleCN: 我们在公交终点站见面。

items.meaning: in a way that ends, especially of a fatal illness
items.meaningCN: 在末端地；末期地，尤指致命疾病（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: able to be ended, especially by notice
items.meaningCN: 可终止的，尤指可通过通知结束（-able 表示“可被”）
items.example: The agreement is terminable on six months' notice.
items.exampleCN: 该协议可在提前六个月通知后终止。

items.meaningCN: 无休止的；长得令人厌烦的（in- 否定“可终止”）
items.exampleCN: 那场会议漫长得没完没了。

items.meaning: to destroy completely, driving something beyond the boundary
items.meaningCN: 灭绝；彻底消灭（ex- 表示“向外、越过边界”）
items.example: The campaign aimed to exterminate the invasive beetle.
items.exampleCN: 这场行动旨在彻底消灭这种入侵甲虫。

items.meaning: the final stop of a route, or an end point
items.meaningCN: 终点站；终点（保留拉丁名词形式）
items.example: The terminus is a ten-minute walk from the market.
items.exampleCN: 终点站离市场步行十分钟。

items.meaning: to end at a stated place
items.meaningCN: 在某一地点终止（at 标记地点）
items.example: The cable terminates at the junction box.

items.meaning: to end with a particular result
items.meaningCN: 以某种结果告终（in 标记结果）
items.example: The march terminated in a peaceful rally.
items.exampleCN: 游行以一场和平集会告终。

items.meaning: to end by means of or with something
items.meaningCN: 以某物结束；以……收尾（with 标记结尾方式）
items.example: The ceremony terminated with a short prayer.
items.exampleCN: 仪式以一段简短的祈祷结束。

latinEntries.meaning: a boundary stone or marker; an end
to set a bound, limit, or end

latinEntries.meaningCN: 有边界的；有限的；已结束的

definition_zh: 刺客；暗杀者
definition_en: a person who kills an important person suddenly and secretly for payment or a cause
core_image: 暗巷阴影里等待目标经过的杀手
scene: 史书里写道，那位将军在检阅途中被藏在人群中的刺客用匕首刺杀。 The assassin waited on the bridge for the duke's carriage.
sceneCN: 这里 assassin 是「刺客」（第 1 个义项：受人指使秘密行凶者）；句意是刺客在桥上等候公爵的马车。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加动词后缀构成，义为「暗杀；行刺」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「暗杀（事件）」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「暗杀的（罕用）」

senses.title: A secret political killer
senses.definition: one who murders a prominent figure by surprise attack
senses.definitionCN: 以突然袭击谋杀显要人物的人
senses.example: History books record the assassin who shot the archduke in Sarajevo.
senses.exampleCN: 史书记载了在萨拉热窝枪击大公的刺客。
senses.why: The word comes from a medieval order whose members, it was said, fortified themselves with hashish before attacks.
senses.whyCN: 该词源自一个中世纪派别，据传其成员行凶前以大麻提神。

senses.title: Any hired or secret killer
senses.definition: any person paid or persuaded to kill secretly
senses.definitionCN: 受雇或受唆使秘密杀人者
senses.example: The novel's assassin never misses his mark.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的杀手弹无虚发。
senses.why: From the political case the word widened to every stealthy contract killer.
senses.whyCN: 从政治案件出发，词义扩展到一切隐秘的雇凶杀手。

intro.en: Assassin comes through French and Italian from Arabic hashshashin, users of hashish, a name given to a medieval sect of political killers.
intro.cn: assassin 经法语、意大利语源自阿拉伯语 hashshāshīn（吸食大麻者），是外界对一个中世纪暗杀派别的称呼。

items.en: Hashshashin meant users of hashish, applied to the Nizari Ismaili order in Persia and Syria.
items.cn: hashshāshīn 意为「服食哈希什者」，用于波斯和叙利亚的尼扎里派。

items.en: Crusader writers popularized stories of drugged killers obeying a hidden master.
items.cn: 十字军编年史作者传播了「服药杀手听命于隐秘主人」的故事。

items.en: Italian assassino carried the word through trade and travel writing.
items.cn: 意大利语 assassino 经商旅与游记传播该词。

items.en: French assassin entered literary use.
items.cn: 法语 assassin 进入文学用语。

items.en: English adopted assassin in the sixteenth century; the verb followed shortly after.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语借入 assassin，动词形式随后出现。

note.en: The word's drug story is colorful but partly legend; what is sure is the Arabic tribal-political source.
note.cn: 「服毒行凶」的故事色彩浓烈但半属传说；可以肯定的是其阿拉伯语的政治派别来源。

entries.definition: to kill a prominent person secretly
entries.definitionCN: 暗杀；行刺

entries.definition: the act of assassinating
entries.definitionCN: 暗杀事件

entries.definition: a predatory insect named for its stealthy strike
entries.definitionCN: 猎蝽（因偷袭得名）

entries.definition: the drug behind the Arabic name
entries.definitionCN: 哈希什（阿拉伯语名称的来源）

entries.definition: similar rhythm, no relation at all

entries.definitionCN: 杀手（泛称）

entries.definitionCN: 职业杀手（口语）

normalIntro.en: Say ass-ass-in: sneaking in like two donkeys' stubbornness bent on one dark deed.
normalIntro.cn: 「额赛星」→联想「暗舍心」：藏身暗舍、心存杀机，即是 assassin（刺客）。

normal.en: Arabic hashshashin: hashish users, the label for a killer sect.
normal.cn: 阿拉伯语 hashshashin：服食哈希什者，对一个暗杀派别的称呼。

normal.en: passed through Italian assassino and French assassin.
normal.cn: 经意大利语 assassino 与法语 assassin 传入。

normal.en: assassinate adds the verb ending -ate.
normal.cn: assassinate 加动词后缀 -ate。

normal.en: political targets are the classic prey.
normal.cn: 政治目标是典型的猎物。

normal.en: an assassin strikes by surprise, not open battle.
normal.cn: 刺客偷袭，不堂堂开战。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow detaching from a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象一个影子从门廊剥离。

abstract.en: Hear one heartbeat of silence before the strike.
abstract.cn: 听见动手前那一下无声的心跳。

abstract.en: See a name struck from a list of the living.
abstract.cn: 看见名单上一个名字被划去。

examples.en: The assassin blended into the festival crowd.
examples.cn: 刺客混入了节日的人群。

examples.en: Her thriller follows an assassin with a conscience.
examples.cn: 她的惊悚小说讲述一个有良知的杀手。

examples.en: Guards searched every visitor for the feared assassin.
examples.cn: 卫兵搜查每位访客，搜寻令人惧怕的刺客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「暗舍星」——隐在暗舍、心藏杀星的杀手，正是 assassin。

root: 阿拉伯语 hashshāshīn（服哈希什者），中世纪尼扎里暗杀派别的诨名，经意大利语、法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: From a sect's nickname to any stealthy killer of prominent people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个派别的诨名，扩展为对一切暗杀显要者的隐秘杀手的称呼。

branches.cn: 围绕一次行凶写就的历史

branches.cn: 作为故事角色的杀手

intro.en: Assassin stands as a lone borrowing; its family grows by English suffixes, not Latin roots.
intro.cn: assassin 是孤立的外来词；其词族靠英语后缀扩展，而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates: the source is Arabic.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词：来源是阿拉伯语。

definition_zh: 掺杂物；掺假用的物质
definition_en: a substance added to something to make it impure or of lower quality
core_image: 一勺白粉悄悄混进整袋奶粉里，袋子没变重多少，东西却坏了
scene: 化验员把样本放进仪器，屏幕上跳出一条多余的曲线。 The lab found an adulterant mixed into the chili powder.
sceneCN: 这里 adulterant 是「掺杂物」（第 1 个义项：被故意混进去以降低纯度的物质）；句意为实验室在辣椒粉里检出了掺杂物。

derivatives.zh: 动词基础形式，义为「掺假；使不纯」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「掺假行为；掺杂」
由动词过去分词转形容词，义为「掺了假的」

senses.title: Substance that spoils purity
senses.definition: a foreign substance mixed into a food, drug or material to make it cheaper or heavier
senses.definitionCN: 混进食品、药品或原料中使其变便宜或变重的外来物质
senses.example: Water is the cheapest adulterant in milk.
senses.exampleCN: 水是牛奶里最便宜的掺杂物。
senses.why: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute', so an adulterant is literally a polluting ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」，所以 adulterant 字面上就是污染性成分。

senses.title: Describing such a substance
senses.definition: serving to adulterate; used of a substance that makes something impure
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容起掺假作用的物质
senses.example: The inspector listed the adulterant agents used by the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员列出了该工厂使用的掺假物质。
senses.why: The noun sense extends into a modifier: the substance defined by its dirty job.
senses.whyCN: 名词义扩展为修饰语：这种物质以它干的脏活来定义。

intro.en: Adulterant comes from Latin adulterare, 'to pollute, to corrupt', from adulter, 'spurious, impure'.
intro.cn: adulterant 来自拉丁语 adulterare（污染、败坏），词根是 adulter（假的、不纯的）。

items.en: Adulter meant 'adulterated, spurious', formed with the prefix ad-, 'toward', on a root meaning 'to pollute'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 adulter 意为「掺假的、假冒的」，由前缀 ad-（朝向）加表示「污染」的词干构成。

items.en: Adulterare was the verb 'to corrupt, to make impure', used of goods and of morals.
items.cn: 动词 adulterare 意为「败坏、使不纯」，既用于货物也用于道德。

items.en: English adopted adulterate in the sixteenth century for corrupting goods.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 adulterate，指对货物做手脚。

items.en: As food regulation grew, adulterant named the specific polluting substance.
items.cn: 随着食品法规兴起，adulterant 专指污染性物质本身。

items.en: Today adulterant appears mostly in food, drug and forensic contexts.
items.cn: 如今 adulterant 多出现在食品、药品与司法检验语境中。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar shape; the second gathers related impurity words.
note.cn: 第一组收词形相近的词；第二组收与「不纯、污染」相关的词。

entries.definition: A grown person; the shared opening is accidental, the roots are unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；开头拼写碰巧相同，词源无关。

entries.definition: Flattering in an excessive way; similar shape, different Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谄媚的」；词形相近，但拉丁词根不同。

entries.definition: The verb from which adulterant is derived; to mix in an impure substance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，adulterant 的来源动词，义为「掺假」。

entries.definition: A polluting substance, usually introduced accidentally.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「污染物」，多指无意混入。

entries.definition: Any substance that makes a material impure.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杂质」，泛指使不纯的成分。

entries.definition: A cheap substance used to bulk out a product.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「填充物」，指用来增量的廉价成分。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pollute root and the lab scene; the abstract hooks picture a white powder and a guilty spoon.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「污染」词根与化验场景；抽象记忆点想象一勺白粉。

normal.en: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」。

normal.en: Adulterate is the verb, adulterant the agent.
normal.cn: adulterate 是动词，adulterant 是那个东西。

normal.en: Adulteration names the practice itself.
normal.cn: adulteration 指掺假这种行径。

normal.en: Adulterated milk is milk with an adulterant.
normal.cn: 掺假牛奶就是混了掺杂物的牛奶。

normal.en: The plural adulterants lists them all.
normal.cn: 复数 adulterants 把它们一并列出。

abstract.en: Picture one bad spoonful spoiling the whole sack.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺坏东西毁掉一整袋。

abstract.en: Picture a lab curve jumping where it should not.
abstract.cn: 想象化验曲线在不该跳的地方跳了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a scale tipped with cheap powder.
abstract.cn: 想象天平被廉价粉末压偏。

examples.en: The lab found an adulterant mixed into the chili powder.
examples.cn: 实验室在辣椒粉里检出了掺杂物。

examples.en: Regulators ban any adulterant that threatens health.
examples.cn: 监管机构禁止任何危害健康的掺杂物。

examples.en: Adulterants make cheap goods look like the real thing.
examples.cn: 掺杂物让廉价货看起来像真货。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额特料」——额外加的料，就是那点见不得光的掺假物。

root: 拉丁语 adulter（假的、不纯的）→ adulterare（污染、败坏）→ 英语 adulterate / adulterant；核心义是「把好东西弄脏的那一点外来物」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the polluting substance itself to its use as a describing word.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从污染性物质本身，走到它作修饰语的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foreign powder slipped into a clean sack
core.cn: 核心意象：偷偷混进净袋里的一把外来粉末

branches.en: The substance that does the dirtying.
branches.cn: 干脏活的那种物质。

branches.en: The word describing any such substance.
branches.cn: 形容这类物质的用语。

branches.en: Both senses center on ruined purity.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕被破坏的纯度。

branches.en: Food and drug tests hunt it down.
branches.cn: 食品药品检测专门缉拿它。

branches.en: Water, starch and dye are classic cases.
branches.cn: 水、淀粉与染料是经典案例。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin pollute root adulter- with the agent ending -ant, and the family gives adulterate and adulteration.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「污染」词根 adulter- 与施动尾 -ant，同族词有 adulterate 与 adulteration。

latinIntro.en: Latin adulter and adulterare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 adulter 与 adulterare 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: n. 暗杀；行刺（尤指政治人物）；（名誉的）毁谤
definition_en: The murder of a prominent person, usually for political reasons; figuratively, the deliberate destruction of a reputation.
core_image: 一声枪响之后，一个位置突然空了
scene: 广播里传来总统遇刺的消息。 The radio reported the assassination of the president.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：assassination 指出于政治等目的杀害重要人物。

derivatives.zh: 暗杀；行刺
刺客；暗杀者

senses.title: The killing of a prominent person
senses.definition: the deliberate murder of a public figure, usually to change or punish a political order
senses.definitionCN: 有意杀害公众人物，通常为了改变或惩罚某种政治秩序
senses.example: The assassination plunged the country into mourning.
senses.exampleCN: 这次暗杀使全国陷入哀悼。
senses.why: What separates this word from murder is the target: the victim matters to many people, so the act is public.
senses.whyCN: 把这个词与 murder 区分开的是目标：受害者对许多人都有分量，所以这一行为是公共性的。

senses.title: The killing of a reputation
senses.definition: a sustained attempt to destroy someone standing, as in the phrase character assassination
senses.definitionCN: 持续地摧毁某人的声望，如「人格毁谤」这一说法
senses.example: The campaign was character assassination, not debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那场攻势是人格毁谤，不是辩论。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the essentials: a chosen target, a planned strike and something that cannot be brought back.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了核心要素：选定的目标、有计划的打击，以及无法挽回的东西。

intro.en: Assassination comes from assassin, traced by the traditional account to Arabic hashshashin, a name applied to a secretive order in Persia and Syria.
intro.cn: assassination 出自 assassin；按传统说法，后者源自阿拉伯语 hashshashin，是对波斯与叙利亚一个秘密教团的称呼。

items.en: The traditional account links the word to a name for a secretive order whose members carried out targeted killings.
items.cn: 传统说法把这个词与一个秘密教团的称号相联，其成员执行有目标的杀害。

items.en: Crusaders brought back stories and the name, and the tale of drug use is now doubted by historians.
items.cn: 十字军带回故事与这个称号，而其中「用药」的说法如今已被史家质疑。

items.en: Medieval Latin assassinus named a hired killer, stripping the word of its sect and keeping the act.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 指受雇的杀手，剥去教团背景，只留下行为本身。

items.en: Italian assassinare turned the noun into a verb meaning to murder a prominent person.
items.cn: 意大利语 assassinare 把名词变成动词，意为杀害重要人物。

items.en: English records the noun from the mid seventeenth century, soon standard in political reporting.
items.cn: 英语从十七世纪中叶起记录这个名词，很快成为政治报道的标准用词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century journalism fixed character assassination for the planned ruin of a name.
items.cn: 十九世纪新闻业固定了 character assassination 一语，指有计划地毁掉一个人的名声。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the assassin family and adds a word that only sounds similar; the near-meaning group grades killings by scale and framing.
note.cn: 形近组保留 assassin 词族，并加上一个只是听着像的词；近义组按规模与说法区分各种杀害。

entries.definition: To murder a prominent person.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害重要人物。

entries.definition: A person who kills for hire or a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 为报酬或信念杀人的刺客。

entries.definition: The killing of many people at once.
entries.definitionCN: 一次杀害许多人。

entries.definition: The state of being intensely interested.
entries.definitionCN: 被强烈吸引的状态。

entries.definition: The unlawful killing of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 非法杀害一个人。

entries.definition: Killing carried out as a penalty.
entries.definitionCN: 作为刑罚实施的处死。

entries.definition: A killing, a word favoured in reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 杀害，报道中偏用的词。

entries.definition: Killing described as mere removal.
entries.definitionCN: 把杀害说成「清除」。

normalIntro.en: Assassination is assassin plus -ation: the act named after the doer, and the doer named after an old order.
normalIntro.cn: assassination 就是 assassin 加 -ation：以行为者命名的行为，而行为者又以一个古老教团命名。

normal.en: Assassin, assassinate, assassination form one chain.
normal.cn: assassin、assassinate、assassination 是一条链。

normal.en: The target must be a public figure.
normal.cn: 目标必须是公众人物。

normal.en: An assassination attempt is a failed one.
normal.cn: an assassination attempt 指未成功的行刺。

normal.en: Character assassination attacks a name, not a body.
normal.cn: character assassination 攻击名声，不是身体。

normal.en: Murder is the wider word, this one is specific.
normal.cn: murder 更宽泛，本词更具体。

abstract.en: Picture one shot and one empty chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一声枪响与一把空椅子。

abstract.en: Imagine a whole street lowering its flags.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街降下半旗。

abstract.en: Think of a name torn down line by line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被一行行撕掉。

examples.en: The plot ended in assassination.
examples.cn: 那场阴谋以暗杀收场。

examples.en: Two assassinations shook the region that year.
examples.cn: 那一年两起暗杀震动了该地区。

examples.en: He called the article character assassination.
examples.cn: 他称那篇文章是人格毁谤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：assassin「刺客」+ -ation「行为」——刺客干的那件事，就是暗杀 assassination。

root: 阿拉伯语 hashshashin 经十字军传闻与中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 变成「受雇杀手」，意大利语 assassinare 转为动词，英语加 -ation 于十七世纪中叶构成 assassination。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses destroy something public and irreplaceable: a person who held a position, and a name that took years to build.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都摧毁某种公共而不可替代之物：占据某个位置的人，以及多年才建立起来的名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shot, and a public place suddenly empty
core.cn: 核心意象：一声枪响之后，一个位置突然空了

branches.en: A radio bulletin and lowered flags.
branches.cn: 一则广播与降下的旗。

branches.en: A plot that ends in one shot.
branches.cn: 以一声枪响收场的阴谋。

branches.en: A name torn down line by line.
branches.cn: 被一行行撕掉的名声。

branches.en: A campaign that is not debate.
branches.cn: 并非辩论的攻势。

branches.en: A chosen public target, struck by plan.
branches.cn: 按计划打击选定的公共目标。

intro.en: Assassination is assassin plus -ation through the verb -ate; the surrounding political vocabulary is built from -al, -ist and -ism.
intro.cn: assassination 是 assassin 经动词后缀 -ate 再加 -ation 构成；周边的政治词汇由 -al、-ist 与 -ism 搭起。

latinIntro.en: The word is Arabic at heart, but Medieval Latin assassinus and assassinare carried it into Europe; Latin caedes, slaughter, names the act beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词内核来自阿拉伯语，但中世纪拉丁语 assassinus 与 assassinare 把它带进欧洲；旁边的拉丁语 caedes「杀戮」指同一行为。

definition_zh: 废除；废止（法律、协议、惯例）
definition_en: to repeal or abolish a law, agreement, or custom formally
core_image: 一纸判词把旧条文划掉作废
scene: 议长敲下木槌，宣布那条过时的税法从今天起不再有效。 The new government abrogated the decades-old treaty.
sceneCN: 这里 abrogate 是「废除」（第 1 个义项：新政府废除旧条约）；句意为新政府废除了那项数十年之久的条约。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「废除；废止」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有废除权的；废止性的」
同根近形词，义为「僭取；擅夺」，与废除义无关

senses.title: To repeal a law or agreement formally
senses.definition: to annul or repeal a law, treaty, or contract by formal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由正式权力机关废止或撤销法律、条约或合同
senses.example: Parliament voted to abrogate the emergency decree.
senses.exampleCN: 议会表决废除了那项紧急法令。
senses.why: Latin ab- (away) plus rogare (to propose a law) means to call a law away, cancelling its force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ab-（离去）加 rogare（提出法案），义为把法律「召离」，使其失效。

senses.title: To end a practice or obligation
senses.definition: to put an end to an established custom or duty as if repealing it
senses.definitionCN: 像废止法条一样终结既有的惯例或义务
senses.example: The reform abrogated centuries of patronage appointments.
senses.exampleCN: 改革终结了延续数百年的恩惠任命。
senses.why: What custom treated as binding is treated as if it were written law, so the repeal verb extends to it.
senses.whyCN: 惯例本有约束力，被当作成文法对待，废除动词随之延伸至惯例。

intro.en: Abrogate comes from Latin abrogatus, past participle of abrogare 'to repeal', from ab- 'away' and rogare 'to propose a law'.
intro.cn: abrogate 来自拉丁语 abrogatus，是 abrogare「废除」的过去分词，由 ab-「离去」加 rogare「提出法案」构成。

items.en: Rogare meant to ask formally, especially to ask the people to accept a law.
items.cn: rogare 义为正式请求，尤指请求民众接受一项法律。

items.en: In Roman usage, abrogare was the technical term for repealing a statute through vote.
items.cn: 在罗马用法中，abrogare 是经表决废止法规的术语。

items.en: Derogare, by contrast, meant only to subtract part of a law; the pair kept distinct legal senses.
items.cn: 与之相对，derogare 只指削减法律的某部分；两者在法律语中分工明确。

items.en: Subrogare meant to put another law in the place of the repealed one.
items.cn: subrogare 指以另一法条取代被废者。

items.en: The word entered English legal and theological writing with the full Roman sense.
items.cn: 十六世纪该词带着完整的罗马法意义进入英语法律与神学著作。

items.en: It stays formal, reserved for laws, treaties, and solemn institutional acts.
items.cn: 如今仍属正式用语，限于法律、条约与庄严的机构行为。

entries.definition: to detract from or partially repeal; Roman law partner of abrogate.
entries.definitionCN: 贬损或部分废止；罗马法中与 abrogate 相对。

entries.definition: to question formally; the asking root without the repealing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式质询；同根但只有「问」义。

entries.definition: to give up a throne or duty; looks close but comes from dicere, not rogare.
entries.definitionCN: 放弃王位或职责；形近但词根是 dicere 而非 rogare。

entries.definition: to withdraw a law officially; the everyday legal partner.
entries.definitionCN: 正式撤回法律；日常法律对应词。

entries.definition: to declare something void from the start, as with a marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告自始无效，如宣告婚姻无效。

entries.definition: to cancel a contract or order retroactively.
entries.definitionCN: 追溯性地取消合同或命令。

entries.definition: to confirm formally; the opposite institutional move.
entries.definitionCN: 正式批准；机构行为上的反向操作。

entries.definition: to put a rule back into force after repeal.
entries.definitionCN: 废除后恢复某规则的效力。

root: 拉丁语 abrogare：ab-（离去）+ rogare（正式提请、立法之问）。在罗马法中特指经表决废止整部法规，与 derogare（部分削减）、subrogare（以新代旧）分工。十六世纪经学术英语进入法律与神学语域，至今保持正式色彩。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: treaties, decrees, and statutes die by formal act.
branches.cn: 文书：条约、法令与法规经正式行为废止。

branches.en: CUSTOMS: patronage and old habits treated as implicit law.
branches.cn: 惯例：恩惠任命与旧习被视作不成文之法。

branches.en: AUTHORITY REQUIRED: only a competent body can abrogate.
branches.cn: 须有权威：唯有适格机构可行废除。

branches.en: WHOLENESS: unlike derogate, the repeal is complete.
branches.cn: 整体性：与 derogate 不同，废除是彻底的。

branches.en: FORMAL REGISTER: everyday speech prefers repeal or scrap.
branches.cn: 正式语域：日常口语更常说 repeal 或 scrap。

definition_en: the official power of a court or authority to hear cases, make decisions or regulate a field, and the area or matters over which that power applies

scene: 两名警官在河边争执，却谁也不肯跨过界碑，因为那段水面不在自己的辖区之内。 Neither officer would cross the boundary stone, because the stretch of water lay outside his jurisdiction.
sceneCN: 这里 jurisdiction 指「某一机关有权处理的地域范围」（第 2 个义项：管辖区域）；句意为两名警官都不肯跨过界碑，因为那段水面不在自己的辖区之内。图中可辨识物件：界碑、河水、警徽、两岸的标记。

senses.title: A court's power to hear a case
senses.titleCN: 法院受理与审判案件的权限
senses.definition: the power of a court to hear a particular kind of case and give a binding decision
senses.definitionCN: 法院受理某一类案件并作出有约束力决定的权力
senses.example: The appeal failed because the tribunal had no jurisdiction over criminal matters.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉失败，因为该裁判所对刑事事项没有管辖权。
senses.why: The word joins ius 'law' to dictio 'a saying': jurisdiction is literally the speaking of law, and only certain courts are granted the right to speak it over certain cases.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 ius「法」与 dictio「宣告」结合起来：管辖权字面上就是「宣告法律」，而只有特定法院被授予就特定案件宣告法律的资格。

senses.title: The area covered
senses.definition: the geographical area within which an authority may act
senses.definitionCN: 某一机关可以行动的地理范围
senses.example: Neither officer would cross the boundary stone, because the stretch of water lay outside his jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警官都不肯跨过界碑，因为那段水面不在自己的辖区之内。
senses.why: Power needs a where as well as a what, so the abstract right is measured onto land, and the boundary becomes the visible form of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 权力既需要「对什么」，也需要「在哪里」，于是抽象权限被丈量到土地上，界线成了这个名词可见的形态。

senses.title: Regulatory power over a field
senses.titleCN: 对某一领域的监管权限
senses.definition: the authority of a public body to set and enforce rules in a particular sector
senses.definitionCN: 公共机构在某一行业设定并执行规则的权力
senses.example: Energy pricing fell within the jurisdiction of the provincial board.
senses.exampleCN: 能源定价属于省委员会的管辖范围。
senses.why: Modern regulators hold powers that were once judicial, and they describe their remit with the same noun because both mean the right to decide authoritatively.
senses.whyCN: 现代监管机构握有曾经属于司法的权力，它们用同一个名词来描述职权范围，因为两者都指权威地作出决定的资格。

senses.title: A state's legal power
senses.titleCN: 国家对人与地的法律权力
senses.definition: the legal competence of a state over persons, property and events connected with its territory
senses.definitionCN: 国家对与其领土相关的人、财产与事件的法律权限
senses.example: The ship was seized in waters under national jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 该船在受国家管辖的水域被扣押。
senses.why: Sovereignty and jurisdiction are not the same: a state may own nothing in a place and still hold the right to try crimes committed there.
senses.whyCN: 主权与管辖权并不相同：一个国家可以在某地没有任何产业，却仍拥有审判在那里发生的罪行的权力。

senses.title: The limits of any authority
senses.titleCN: 任何权限的边界（在权限内/越权）
senses.definition: the scope within which a person or body may properly act, often invoked when someone has gone beyond it
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某机构可以正当行动的界限，常在有人越界时被援引
senses.example: The inspector was told that the question lay outside her jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 有人告知这位稽查员，该问题超出她的权限。
senses.why: The noun is used negatively as much as positively: saying that something is outside a jurisdiction is the standard way to refuse to act.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词的否定用法与肯定用法一样多：说某事「不在管辖之内」，是拒绝行动的惯常说法。

senses.title: Competence between states
senses.titleCN: 国际法上国家之间的管辖权限
senses.definition: the competence of one state to exercise authority, especially criminal jurisdiction, over acts with a foreign element
senses.definitionCN: 一国对有外国因素的行为行使权威（尤其是刑事管辖）的权限
senses.example: Under universal jurisdiction, any state may try the case.
senses.exampleCN: 依普遍管辖权，任何国家都可以审理该案。
senses.why: Where there is no world court, the noun is used to divide competence between sovereigns, and the dividing line is negotiated rather than drawn by a single legislator.
senses.whyCN: 在没有世界法院的地方，这个名词用来在主权国家之间划分权限，而那条分界线是协商出来的，并非由单一立法者画出。

senses.title: The authority of a church court
senses.definition: the power of an ecclesiastical court or bishop to decide matters of doctrine and discipline
senses.definitionCN: 教会法庭或主教就教义与纪律事项作出决定的权力
senses.example: The marriage case was returned to the church's own jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩婚姻案件被交回教会自己的管辖范围。
senses.why: Church courts held this power long before royal ones, so the noun entered legal language with an ecclesiastical owner already in place.
senses.whyCN: 教会法庭掌握这项权力远早于王室法庭，因此这个名词进入法律语言时，早已有一个教会的所有者。

senses.title: Exercising or declining it
senses.titleCN: 行使或拒绝行使管辖权
senses.definition: the act by which a court takes up a matter, or formally refuses to
senses.definitionCN: 法院接手某一事项、或正式拒绝接手的动作
senses.example: The court declined jurisdiction and left the parties to arbitrate.
senses.exampleCN: 法院拒绝行使管辖权，让当事人自行仲裁。
senses.why: Rights are exercised by acts, so the noun also names the moment of taking or refusing a case, which is why lawyers speak of assuming and declining jurisdiction.
senses.whyCN: 权利通过行为行使，因此这个名词也命名接手或拒绝案件的时刻，律师所谓「取得管辖」与「拒绝管辖」即由此而来。

intro.en: Jurisdiction comes from Latin iurisdictio, from ius 'law, right' plus dictio 'a saying', from dicere 'to speak'. It entered English through French in the medieval period.
intro.cn: jurisdiction 来自拉丁 iurisdictio，由 ius「法、权利」加 dictio「宣告」（出自 dicere「说」）构成。它在中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ius meant law in the sense of right and binding custom, as distinct from lex, an enacted statute; the distinction matters for this word's relatives.
items.cn: ius 指作为权利与有约束力习俗的法，与 lex「被制定的法令」相区别；这一区别对这个词的同族词很重要。

items.en: Dicere meant to say or to declare publicly; dictio is the act of saying, so the compound names the public declaration of what is right.
items.cn: dicere 意为说、公开宣告；dictio 是「说」这一行为，因此这个复合词命名对何者为正当的公开宣告。

items.en: Iurisdictio in Roman law meant the magistrate's function of stating the law for a case, not the whole power of a modern court.
items.cn: iurisdictio 在罗马法中指长官为一案宣告法律这一职能，而非现代法院的全部权力。

items.en: Medieval church and royal courts both claimed the right to declare the law in their own spheres, and the noun was fixed to that division of competence.
items.cn: 中世纪教会法庭与王室法庭都主张在各自领域宣告法律的资格，这个名词被固定到这种权限划分上。

items.en: Modern states extended the noun to regulators and to international competence, so the word now covers any bounded right to decide.
items.cn: 现代国家把这个名词扩展到监管机构与国际权限，如今它覆盖任何有边界的决定权。

items.en: The English first date is approximate: the borrowing is medieval, but the earliest citation in legal French and English is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 英语首见年代为约数：借入发生在中世纪，但法律法语与英语中的最早书证没有精确年代。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin ius but differs in what it names; the second group names neighbouring kinds of authority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁 ius，但命名的对象不同；第二组是相邻的权限种类。

entries.definition: The adjective for anything concerning jurisdiction, especially in procedural objections.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与管辖权有关的事项，尤用于程序异议。

entries.definition: A scholar of law, from ius; it names a person who studies law, not a power.
entries.definitionCN: 法学家，出自 ius；它指研究法律的人，而非一种权力。

entries.definition: The theory or study of law, from ius plus prudentia 'knowledge'; it names learning, not the right to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 关于法的理论或研究，由 ius 加 prudentia「知识」构成；命名学问，而非决定权。

entries.definition: From iurare 'to swear', not ius: a sworn body of citizens, so its resemblance to jurisdiction is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 iurare「宣誓」而非 ius：指宣誓的公民团体，因此与 jurisdiction 的相似是假象。

entries.definition: From iudex, built on ius plus dicere, a cousin of the same stock but naming the person.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 iudex，由 ius 与 dicere 构成，同源但命名的是那个人。

entries.definition: Any recognised power to act or decide, with no territorial or subject limit built in.
entries.definitionCN: 任何被承认的行动或决定权，不含地域或事项的固有界限。

entries.definition: In law and diplomacy, the capacity of a body to act; it overlaps with jurisdiction but stresses capacity rather than territory.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律与外交中，指机构行事的能力；与 jurisdiction 重叠，但强调能力而非地域。

entries.definition: The locality where a case is tried, a question of convenience rather than of power.
entries.definitionCN: 审判案件的地点，属便利问题，而非权力问题。

entries.definition: The commission given to a body by a superior authority, which defines what it may do.
entries.definitionCN: 上级授予某机构的任务与权限，界定它可以做什么。

entries.definition: The scope of a statute or document, a matter of coverage rather than of power.
entries.definitionCN: 法令或文书的覆盖范围，属涵盖问题而非权力问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin law and saying, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「法」与「宣告」、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Ius is law and dictio is a saying, so jurisdiction is the saying of law, the right to declare it in a given case.
normal.cn: ius 是法，dictio 是宣告，因此管辖就是「宣告法律」，即就某一案件宣告法律的资格。

normal.en: The family runs jurisdiction, jurisdictional, jurisdictionally, jurist and jurisprudence.
normal.cn: 同族词有 jurisdiction、jurisdictional、jurisdictionally、jurist 与 jurisprudence。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the limits: within the jurisdiction of, outside the court's jurisdiction, exercise jurisdiction over.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出界限：在……管辖之内、超出法院管辖、对……行使管辖。

normal.en: Ius and lex were different words in Latin: the first is right, the second is statute, which is why jurisdiction and legal do not share a root.
normal.cn: 拉丁语中 ius 与 lex 是两个词：前者是权利，后者是法令，因此 jurisdiction 与 legal 并不同根。

normal.en: A boundary stone is the noun made visible, since every power needs a where.
normal.cn: 界碑是这个名词的可见形态，因为每一种权力都需要一个「在哪里」。

abstract.en: Picture two officers standing on either side of a stone, each unwilling to lift a foot.
abstract.cn: 想象两名警官站在界碑两侧，谁都不肯抬脚。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone that only works inside one room, however loud the speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象一支只在某个房间内起作用的麦克风，无论说话多大声。

abstract.en: Picture a key cut for one door in a street of identical doors.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，只配得上同一条街上众多相同门中的一扇。

examples.en: The case was moved to a court with proper jurisdiction.
examples.cn: 该案被移送到有适当管辖权的法院。

examples.en: Local police have no jurisdiction beyond the county line.
examples.cn: 地方警察在县界之外没有管辖权。

examples.en: The treaty allows jurisdiction to be shared in cross-border cases.
examples.cn: 该条约允许在跨境案件中共享管辖权。

root: 拉丁 ius「法、权利」+ dictio「宣告」（出自 dicere「说」）→ iurisdictio「宣告法律、司法职能」→ 法语 → 英语 jurisdiction。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one boundary stone: it marks a court's cases, a district's ground, a regulator's sector, a state's reach, any authority's limit, the line between nations, a church's sphere, and the moment of taking or refusing a case.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一块界碑：它标出法院能审的案件、地区的土地、监管者的行业、国家的触及范围、任何权限的界限、国家之间的线、教会的领域，以及接手或拒绝案件的时刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone in the ground with an officer on either side, neither crossing.
core.cn: 核心意象：地上立着一块石头，两侧各有一名警官，谁都不越过去。

branches.en: POWER AND ITS EXERCISE: the right to hear and the act of taking a case are the same power asleep and awake.
branches.cn: 权力与行使：受理资格与接手案件的动作，是同一权力的睡与醒。

branches.en: THREE MAPS: a district, an industry and a state all draw the same boundary at different scales.
branches.cn: 三张地图：地区、行业与国家在不同尺度上画出同一条界线。

branches.en: THE LIMIT AS A REFUSAL: the noun is most often used to say that something is not mine to decide.
branches.cn: 界限即拒绝：这个名词最常用来表示「此事不归我决定」。

branches.en: BETWEEN SOVEREIGNS: without a world legislature, competence is negotiated rather than granted.
branches.cn: 主权之间：没有世界立法者，权限靠协商而非授予。

branches.en: THE OLDER COURT: a church court holds the same right to declare, and the noun needs no change.
branches.cn: 更早的法庭：教会法庭握有同样的宣告权，名词无需改动。

intro.en: Jurisdiction is a Latin compound of 'law' and 'saying', and both halves remain visible in English relatives.
intro.cn: jurisdiction 是拉丁语「法」与「宣告」的复合，两半在英语同族词里仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius gives jurist, jurisprudence and justice; dicere gives dictate, diction and verdict; the compound iurisdictio gives jurisdiction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ius 提供 jurist、jurisprudence 与 justice；dicere 提供 dictate、diction 与 verdict；复合词 iurisdictio 给出 jurisdiction。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 jurisprudence，指学问而非权力。
